name: PostHog
description: Product analytics, funnels, session replay and feature flags.
usage: Track product events with `capture("event", { ...props })`. Name events in snake_case with a past-tense verb (`signup_completed`, `kit_installed`) and identify the user with `identify(id)` after login. Never send sensitive personal data as properties. On the client: `import posthog from "posthog-js"`; on the server: `getPostHogServer()` from `@/lib/posthog-server` (call `await client.shutdown()` when done).
setupTasks: PostHog: copy the Project API key into `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` if you use the EU region.
PostHog: agree with the user on the product's 5–10 key events before instrumenting (`instrument-product-analytics` skill).

name: PostHog
description: Product analytics and feature flags in the app.
usage: Track product events with `capture("event", { ...props })`. Name events in snake_case with a past-tense verb (`signup_completed`, `kit_installed`) and identify the user with `identify(id)` after login. Never send sensitive personal data as properties. Use the `usePostHog()` hook inside components.
setupTasks: PostHog: put the project key in `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY`.
PostHog: wrap the app in `<PostHogProvider client={posthog}>` in `src/app/_layout.tsx` when `posthog` isn't null.

name: PostHog
description: Events and feature flags from your API.
usage: Track product events with `capture("event", { ...props })`. Name events in snake_case with a past-tense verb (`signup_completed`, `kit_installed`) and identify the user with `identify(id)` after login. Never send sensitive personal data as properties. Use `getPostHog()` from `src/lib/posthog.ts` and call `await client.shutdown()` at the end of each request in serverless environments.
setupTasks: PostHog: put the project key in `POSTHOG_KEY`.

name: Better Auth
description: Auth in your own database: email, OAuth, 2FA, organizations.
usage: Read the session on the server with `auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() })` (from `@/lib/auth`) and on the client with `authClient.useSession()` (from `@/lib/auth-client`). Add providers and plugins in `src/lib/auth.ts`.

writeFiles.content:

export const authClient = createAuthClient();

setupTasks: Better Auth: generate a secret with `openssl rand -base64 32` and put it in `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`.

Better Auth: create its tables with `npx auth@latest generate --output src/db/auth-schema.ts`, export them from `src/db/schema.ts` and apply the migration (`npm run db:generate && npm run db:migrate`).

name: Clerk
description: Managed auth with ready-made login components.
usage: Protect routes in `src/proxy.ts` with `clerkMiddleware` and read the user with `auth()` / `currentUser()` from `@clerk/nextjs/server`. Use its components (`<SignInButton>`, `<UserButton>`) instead of building login forms.
setupTasks: Clerk: create an application at clerk.com and copy its keys into `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`.
Clerk: wrap the contents of `<body>` in `src/app/layout.tsx` with `<ClerkProvider>` (from `@clerk/nextjs`).

description: Typed ORM and SQL migrations on Postgres (Neon, Supabase, local).
usage: The schema lives in `src/db/schema.ts` and the client in `src/db/index.ts` (`import { db } from "@/db"`). After changing the schema: `npm run db:generate` and `npm run db:migrate`. Never edit migrations that were already applied.

name: Stripe
description: Payments, subscriptions and billing.
usage: The client is in `src/lib/stripe.ts` (server only). Always verify webhook signatures with `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and treat webhooks as the source of truth for payment and subscription state.
setupTasks: Stripe: copy the test secret key into `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and create the webhook (or use `stripe listen`) for `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

name: Resend
description: Transactional email with a simple API.
usage: Send from the server with `getResend().emails.send({ from, to, subject, html })` (from `src/lib/email.ts`). Never expose `RESEND_API_KEY` to the client.
setupTasks: Resend: create an API key at resend.com, put it in `RESEND_API_KEY` and verify your domain to send from it.

name: Zustand
description: Minimal global state with hooks, no providers.
usage: Each store lives in `src/stores/` and is created with `create()`. Read only what you need with a selector (`useStore((s) => s.x)`) to avoid extra re-renders. Use local React state for anything that isn't shared.

usage: Define atoms in `src/atoms/` with `atom()` and use them with `useAtom`. Prefer small and derived atoms over one big object.

name: SWR
description: Requests with caching and revalidation, by Vercel.
usage: Fetch data with `useSWR(key, fetcher)` and use the `fetcher` from `src/lib/fetcher.ts`. Never `fetch` inside `useEffect`.

name: TanStack Query
description: Caching and loading states for requests in Vue.
usage: Use `useQuery` and `useMutation` from `@tanstack/vue-query` for data that changes on the client; for page data use Nuxt's `useFetch`.

name: TanStack Query
description: Caching and loading states for requests in Svelte.
usage: Use `createQuery` from `@tanstack/svelte-query` for data that changes on the client; for page data use SvelteKit's `load` functions.

description: Fast forms with schema validation.
usage: Every form uses `useForm` with `zodResolver(schema)`; the Zod schema is the single source of validation rules and types.

name: Zod
description: Typed schemas to validate incoming data.
usage: Validate every piece of outside data (forms, APIs, environment variables) with a Zod schema and infer the types with `z.infer`.

name: SQLModel
description: Database and API models in one, from FastAPI's creator.
usage: Models inherit from `SQLModel` (with `table=True` for tables). Use `get_session` from `app/db.py` as a FastAPI dependency. It uses SQLite by default; in production set `DATABASE_URL`.

writeFiles.content:
import os
from collections.abc import Iterator

from sqlmodel import Session, SQLModel, create_engine

engine = create_engine(os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:///./app.db"))


def create_tables() -> None:
    SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)


def get_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session

name: pytest-django
description: Django tests with pytest and its fixtures.

DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = config.settings
python_files = tests.py test_*.py

name: GitHub Actions
description: Checks and runs the Django tests on every push and PR.
usage: The workflow is in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`manage.py check` and `manage.py test`). Keep `requirements.txt` up to date.

writeFiles.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: python manage.py check
      - run: python manage.py test

name: pgx (Postgres)
description: The most widely used Postgres driver for Go, with connection pooling.
usage: Open the pool once with `connectDB` (from `db.go`) at startup and pass it to the handlers. Use parameterized queries (`$1`), never concatenate SQL.

name: testify
description: Readable assertions for Go tests.
usage: Use `assert` for checks that continue and `require` for those that must stop the test. Tests next to the code (`*_test.go`).

name: golangci-lint
description: Many Go linters in one, with a single config.
usage: Check with `golangci-lint run` before finishing a task; the config is in `.golangci.yml`.

linters:

    - govet

    - revive

name: Docker
description: A minimal image with the compiled binary.
usage: Build with `docker build -t api .` and run with `docker run -p 8080:8080 api`. The final image only contains the binary.

COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /app .

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static
COPY --from=build /app /app
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/app"]

name: Essential skills
description: Plan before coding, debug methodically, verify before calling anything done, review the code, keep it secure and improve the architecture. Works in any project.
usage: Before writing anything non-trivial, clarify what's wanted (`brainstorming`, or `grill-me` when the request is ambiguous), write a plan (`writing-plans`) and follow it (`executing-plans`). When something fails, use `systematic-debugging` before touching code. Never say something works without checking it (`verification-before-completion`). Ask for a review when a piece is done (`requesting-code-review`), weigh each comment before applying it (`receiving-code-review`) and close the work with `finishing-a-development-branch`. Anything that handles user input, auth, secrets or external data follows `security-and-hardening`. When code gets hard to change, propose improvements with `improve-codebase-architecture`. If you need a skill you don't have, look for it with `find-skills`.

name: Lemon Squeezy
description: Payments and subscriptions with taxes handled (merchant of record).
usage: Call `setupLemonSqueezy()` (from `src/lib/lemonsqueezy.ts`) before using the SDK, server-side only. Verify webhook signatures with `LEMONSQUEEZY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and treat webhooks as the source of truth.
setupTasks: Lemon Squeezy: create an API key and a store in test mode and fill in the `LEMONSQUEEZY_*` variables.

name: Polar
description: Payments and subscriptions for developers, with taxes handled.
usage: Use the client from `src/lib/polar.ts` on the server only; in development it points to the sandbox. Treat webhooks as the source of truth for payment state.
setupTasks: Polar: create an access token at sandbox.polar.sh and put it in `POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

name: Paddle
description: Global payments and subscriptions with Paddle as the merchant of record.
usage: Use the client from `src/lib/paddle.ts` on the server only (sandbox in development). Verify webhooks with `PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
setupTasks: Paddle: create a sandbox account, generate an API key and put it in `PADDLE_API_KEY`.

name: Mercado Pago
description: Payments in Latin America: cards, bank transfers and local methods.
usage: Use the config from `src/lib/mercadopago.ts` on the server only (`new Preference(mercadoPago)` to create a checkout). Confirm every payment through notifications (webhooks), not the redirect.

name: Design pack
description: A visual direction with character, polished details, accessibility and purposeful animation. The most-used design skills right now.
usage: Before designing a screen, pick a clear visual direction with `frontend-design` (avoid the generic look). To polish and audit what's built, use `impeccable`. Review interface details with `web-design-guidelines` and make every screen usable with a keyboard and a screen reader, with enough contrast, following `accessibility` (WCAG 2.2). For palettes, typography and UI patterns, consult `ui-ux-pro-max`, and for animation and interaction, follow `emil-design-eng`.

name: Mobile design pack
description: Polished native interfaces: visual direction, iOS and Android conventions, and fluid animation.
usage: Pick palettes, typography and screen patterns for your stack (SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter) with `ui-ux-pro-max`, follow each platform's conventions with `mobile-native` and `apple-design`, and design animations with `emil-design-eng`.
